title: To-do view
description: What the manager works out for each to-do and for the To-dos list (#10226, docs/design/proposals/todos-redesign.md 3.3, 3.7, 6.1, 6.3): the row's view and its asks, the places and the counts. The hub only adds counts up and merges places; the cases are in spec/fixtures/todo-view and spec/fixtures/todo-counts.

TodoPhase.description: The to-do's state in the domain (proposal 6.3): needs_you, the owner has to act; working, Persona or an Agent works on it now; waiting, it waits on something named; ready, finished work nobody has ticked; todo, nobody works on it and nothing waits; someday, the owner put it off; done, closed. done holds exactly when the to-do is closed, and a start that failed reads as open. Open: a newer hub may send other values.

TodoListSection.description: Where the list draws the row, in the list's order (proposal 3.4): needs_you; can_wait, folded at the foot of Needs you, listed but not counted; working; waiting; todo; just_finished, open work finished and not ticked, and closed work not seen yet within 24 hours; someday; done. Open: a newer hub may send other values.

TodoReason.description: Why the row is where it is: the row of proposal 6.3 that placed it (docs/design/proposals/todos-redesign.md 3.4 and 6.3 say which reasons each section holds). Inactivity is a mark (TodoSummary.inactive), not a reason. Open: a newer hub may send other values.

TodoLine.description: The row's second line as a key and its arguments, never words: each client says it in its own language (spec/fixtures/todo-view/README.md lists every key and its arguments).

key.description: Stable: never renamed or reused. A client that does not know the key draws no line.

args.description: The key's arguments by name, all strings. A time is an absolute RFC 3339 time, never one relative to now, so the list's bytes stay the same while time passes. Absent when the key takes none.

TodoStepCount.description: The steps of a to-do, the to-dos whose part_of names it: how many are closed, of how many.

done.description: Steps closed; a step whose start failed counts as open.

TodoRunRef.description: An Agent session working for the to-do (a run), by its ids and its title; never its runtime, engine, model or folder.

machine_id.description: The machine the session runs on.

title.description: The session's title as the session list has it, else as the to-do's link recorded it; absent when neither has one.

OwnerAskKind.description: What an ask wants from the owner. The to-do's own asks: decision, verify (Check the result), retry (a start that failed), signin, steps_proposed, duplicate. A run's asks: question, plan, tool (an approval), secret, form. Open: a newer hub may send other values.

OwnerAskHome.description: Where the ask's full card lives (proposal 3.7): todo, on the to-do's page under its state line; run, at the foot of the run's session. Every other place that shows the ask is a door to that home.

OwnerAskRisk.description: How risky answering an ask is (proposal 3.7, decision 4(a)): safe, the row, the card or a push may answer it in place; open, it cannot be undone, other people will see it or what it asks needs a look, so the owner answers it after a look, on its page or at its run. The manager's rule: a decision is open when why only the owner decides is irreversible or visible_to_others, or Persona would take it at a deadline that cannot be undone; a retry is safe; a run's card is safe when a notification may answer it too (one question with options and no fields, not from a Just me turn or a health conversation) and its asker did not say going ahead cannot be undone, and anything else a run asks is open (a question in words, several questions, a dialog on the screen, a plan, a tool approval, a form, a secret, or a run whose card the hub does not hold). Open: a newer hub may send other values, which clients read as open.

OwnerAskLockscreen.description: What a push about the ask may offer on the lock screen (proposal 3.7): answer, its answers as actions, each needing the phone unlocked; open_only, no action, a tap opens it. open_only exactly when the risk is open. Open: a newer hub may send other values, which clients read as open_only.

OwnerAskOption.description: One option of a decision, as its card lists it.

label.description: The option in its card's words; an answer names it.

leads_to.description: What choosing it leads to, in one line; absent when the ask did not say.

OwnerAsk.description: One ask that holds the to-do in Needs you or Can wait: the to-do's own (home todo) or one of its runs' (home run), with how risky answering it is and what a push about it may offer on the lock screen. Its state (answered, held for Undo) comes with answering in place.

id.description: Unique within the row and never reused for a later ask, so what a client keeps by id (an answer, a Later) never lands on a new question. The same while the ask is open, though a hub restart may give an open run's ask a new one, which clients take as a new ask. Opaque to clients (spec/fixtures/todo-view/README.md says how the hub forms it).

round.description: The ask round an answer is for, opaque: sent back as it is (today the asked_at the accept route takes). Absent for an ask with no round (a start that failed, a run's ask).

text.description: What it asks, in the words it was asked in ("Which ryokan?"); absent when nothing says.

run.description: The run that asks; only on a run's ask.

recommend.description: The label of the option the hub recommends; absent when none is.

options.description: A decision's options, the recommended one first; absent when the ask has none.

can_wait.description: It can wait for the briefing: listed under Can wait, not counted. Written only when true.

default_at.description: When Persona takes the recommendation unless the owner answers first; absent when it never does.

risk.description: How risky answering it is. Absent from an older manager: clients read it as open.

lockscreen.description: What a push about it may offer on the lock screen. Absent from an older manager: clients read it as open_only.

interaction.description: The id of the run's pending card this ask is (the session's own before Persona's card about its turn, then the oldest), answered through POST /api/v1/interactions/{id}/resolve; only on a run's ask, and absent while the hub holds no card for the run (its kind is then question).

TodoSummary.description: The view of a to-do: the row's `view` on GET /api/v1/todos and GET /api/v1/todos/{id}. The manager works it out from the to-do, its runs' sessions, its asks and the time, so every client draws the same row without rules of its own (proposal 6.1, 6.3). A row without it comes from an older manager and is drawn as before; so is a row whose section or reason the client does not know.

line.description: Line 2 of the row; absent when there is nothing to say (a plain To do row).

since.description: When the reason began (the ask, the failure, the park, the close…); absent when nothing says.

next_change_at.description: The next moment time alone changes this view (24 hours in Just finished, 48 hours to the Inactive mark, a Someday date): a client files the row again then, without the hub. Absent when only new facts change it.

rank.description: The row's place in its section among the rows of its list, 0 first (proposal 3.4 "Within a section").

seen.description: The owner looked at it since it got where it is (docs/assistant/todo-status-sop.md "Seen"). Written only when true.

inactive.description: The Inactive mark: when activity stopped, on a task nothing has moved for 48 hours that no other rule places. Absent while it is active.

can_wait.description: In Can wait: it needs the owner but can wait, and is not counted. Written only when true.

asks.description: The asks that hold the row in Needs you or Can wait, the most urgent first; absent when none does.

steps.description: Its steps; absent when it has none.

TodoPlaceKind.description: What kind of place a To-dos place is (proposal 3.3): all (All To-dos), today, upcoming, or a project's. Open: a newer hub may send other values.

TodoPlace.description: One place of the To-dos sidebar: All To-dos, Today, Upcoming, or a knowledge-base project with open to-dos.

title.description: The project's title; "" for all, today and upcoming, which each client names in its own language.

project.description: The project's slug; only on a project's place.

needs_you.description: The place's part of TodoCounts.needs_you, counted the same way; 0 for today and upcoming, which draw no count.

manager.description: The manager the place belongs to, stamped by the hub when it merges several managers' places; absent in a manager's own answer.

TodoCounts.description: The numbers of the To-dos list (proposal 3.7), on GET /api/v1/todos and GET /api/v1/todos/places. Across managers the hub adds them up field by field and key by key.

open.description: Open to-dos except Someday: every to-do that is not closed (a start that failed counts), in any section but Someday.

needs_you.description: N: the to-dos in the Needs you section, each once however many of its runs ask; Can wait and quiet tasks are not counted. The To-dos row's badge, the bar's Needs you and the Needs you header show it.

in_progress.description: The rows of Working and Waiting; Just finished is listed at the foot of In progress but not counted.

sections.description: Rows per section, every section named, 0 included, so the bytes stay stable and the hub adds maps up key by key. Quiet tasks count here as the rows they are.

TodoPlaces.description: The answer of GET /api/v1/todos/places: the places, and the counts of the whole list.

places.description: all, today and upcoming, then one place for each project with open to-dos, by slug.

counts.description: The counts of All To-dos, as GET /api/v1/todos answers them.
